correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired claim and proof. For disjoint matched pairs, a first-return comparison forces the first interior empty and an end-symbol comparison forces the second empty; the intervening word then commutes with (), hence is a run of leaves at that same parent. In the nested case irreducibility forces the outer vertex unary, and cancelling its unique child's delimiters reduces to the shorter nested comparison, with the parent-child base case immediate. The collision links form paths (leaf runs cannot meet a unary link). Counting their components gives n-D=U+L. The forest grammar assigns u exactly when a vertex has just one child, or a leaf is appended after a leaf; eliminating T=F_L=zF/(1+z-uz) gives the quadratic and its triangular coefficient recursion. A deepest leaf forces U+L>=1 for n>=2. At u=0 the solution is 1+z, and the linear coefficient in u is z^2(2+z)/(1-z-z^2); n>=2 has tail 2,3,5,...; a single collision path gives only the two stated minimal words. Independently generated 23,713 nonempty Dyck words at sizes 1–10 by choosing and checking up-step positions; computed pair matches by first returns and checked all pairwise collision predictions and the quadratic coefficients by integer interpolation.
residual_risks: Finite replay is corroboration; the unbounded sizes and formal-series claim follow from the proof. No arbitrary up/down erasure or multiple erasure extension is claimed.
